git_note: plus uncommitted working-tree changes; see repository_changes in experiments/006
question: Is the OmniDocBench aggregate score measuring the pipeline, or the OCR language configuration?
independent_variable: ocr_languages only — configs otherwise byte-identical (verified by diff)

baseline_config.note: repository default, tuned for the private Vietnamese corpus

candidate_config.note: EasyOCR cannot serve ch_sim and vi from one reader (vi is in latin_g2, ch_sim in zh_sim_g2)

execution.candidate_contention: CONTENDED (co-tenant job; device:auto classified GPU PROTECTED and selected CPU)
execution.why: GPU and CPU outputs were shown byte-identical in experiment 006 (0.000 px bbox delta), so accuracy is device-independent; only timing is affected by contention.

verdict.summary: Chinese improves substantially and the aggregate improves 25.9%, confirming that the original score was dominated by a language-configuration mismatch rather than a pipeline defect. However English regresses 43.6% and English table structure collapses from 0.715 to 0.000, so a single global OCR language set is not adequate for a multilingual corpus.
verdict.conclusion_for_the_project: Do NOT change the repository default: ['en','vi'] remains correct for the private corpus. The finding is that a benchmark must not inherit a corpus-tuned OCR language config, and that per-document language selection is the real fix.

limitations: 18 pages, one run per configuration, no variance estimate
table_en has n=3 — the 0.715 -> 0.000 collapse is dramatic but on a very small sample
candidate run was CPU-contended; its timing is not a benchmark
Chinese remains at 0.7354 edit distance — much better, but still poor in absolute terms
